name: Ferroelectric Shatter Sidearm FESA-2 'Gravel'
description:
The Ferroelectric Shatter Sidearm generates a localized ferroelectric inversion pulse within a magnetically confined payload of ceramic-metallic composite microbeads — roughly 400 per charge — held in suspension inside the barrel chamber. When fired, the inversion pulse causes each microbead to undergo rapid piezoelectric expansion at an individually offset frequency, creating a cascade of asymmetric fractures across the entire payload simultaneously. The result is not a spray of intact pellets but a cloud of irregularly fractured shards, each tumbling along a slightly different vector, expanding outward in a pattern more akin to a shattering dinner plate than a conventional shotgun spread.

The FESA-2's lethality is deceptive at a glance — it looks like a stubby, unremarkable sidearm, slightly bulbous at the muzzle. At close range, the fracture-cascade cloud creates wound profiles that confound standard trauma treatment, as fragments arrive at skin at varying angles and velocities, defeating layered soft armor by exploiting gaps between impact zones. At medium range the cloud disperses enough to be largely non-lethal, making it a weapon with an unusually sharp lethality curve. ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS markets it as a 'dynamic area denial sidearm,' which is corporate language for a weapon that is devastating in corridors and useless in open fields.

The FESA-2 earned its street name 'Gravel' not from its payload but from the sound it makes on discharge — a dry, grinding crack rather than a conventional report, as if someone snapped a handful of stones. It is a compact weapon favored by operators who work in enclosed environments: ship interiors, server vaults, transit tunnels. The fracture pattern leaves a distinctive wound signature that forensic teams in GLMZ refer to informally as a 'gravel stamp.'
legality: Prohibited in civilian contexts; licensed for contracted security and military units
specifications:
effective range: Lethal: 0–6 meters; suppression: 6–14 meters
payload per charge: ~400 ceramic-metallic composite microbeads
charges per magazine: 8
weight: 1.1 kg loaded
dimensions: 22 cm length, 9 cm muzzle width
power source: Integrated ferroelectric capacitor, charges from standard sidearm rail
armor interaction: Defeats soft armor at close range via distributed impact; ineffective against rigid plate
tactical_use: Standard deployment is as a close-quarters backup weapon for operators breaching confined spaces. Often paired with a primary that handles open engagement. Some users fire a Gravel round into a doorway before entering to suppress occupants without full lethal commitment. Tunnel security teams in GLMZ's underground infrastructure districts carry it as a primary for exactly this reason. A known tactic is the 'double door' — fire into a room, wait for the sound of impacts, then breach while targets are disoriented.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's labyrinthine sub-infrastructure — the transit tunnels, server crawlways, and maintenance corridors that form the city's unglamorous skeleton — the Gravel has become a symbol of the workers and security personnel who live and operate in those spaces. Tunnel gangs prize it as a status weapon precisely because it's useless above-ground; owning one signals that you belong to the underground world. Surface-level street culture views it with mild contempt for this reason, calling it a 'mole gun.'
known_users: GLMZ Transit Authority armed response units
story_hooks: A series of killings in the transit tunnels all bear the gravel stamp wound signature, but the FESA-2 units licensed to that district are all accounted for. Someone is running an unlicensed unit — or ARCTURUS has a leak in its supply chain.

A tunnel gang leader is found dead with a gravel stamp, killed by their own weapon. The sidearm is missing. Their second-in-command insists it was stolen during a deal, but the meeting location was a dead end with no exits.

ARCTURUS quietly updates the FESA-2 firmware, adding a remote disable feature. Operators who discover this are furious — and one of them is planning to make the update public in the most dramatic way possible.

A forensic investigator builds a career on identifying gravel stamp wounds — until a case comes in where the wound profile matches a FESA-2 but the victim was killed in a location physically impossible to reach with one.
related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Combat Exoskeleton Lite CEL-3

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, distinctly bulbous sidearm with an oversized muzzle that dominates its profile. The barrel swells to nearly the width of the grip, giving it an almost organic, bulging appearance — like a water droplet frozen mid-fall. The overall shape is squat and utilitarian, lacking the sleek lines of conventional firearms. At first glance it reads as crude, almost homemade, until the precision engineering becomes apparent.
physical_description.dimensions: 22 cm length overall; 9 cm muzzle width; grip approximately 4 cm wide; barrel chamber depth ~8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively dense and balanced despite compact size. The 1.1 kg load sits low in the hand due to the ferroelectric capacitor core, creating a front-heavy feel that demands grip discipline. Not unwieldy, but demands respect — the weight distribution suggests contained power.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite frame with steel internal lattice; ferroelectric chamber walls are tungsten-composite; magnetic suspension housing is titanium alloy to withstand inversion pulse stress
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel accents around the capacitor housing. The muzzle bell shows a subtle bronze-tinted anodization — functional rather than decorative, likely a thermal dissipation coating. Wear patterns are precise and deliberate, not accidental.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray primary with gunmetal steel secondary; bronze-gold accents at muzzle rim and capacitor vents; minimal branding in matte silver
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with slight tacti-knurling on the forward section; the wraparound grip shows a crosshatch pattern that provides secure purchase even in wet or gloved conditions. Slightly warm to the touch due to capacitor proximity.
distinctive_features: Bulbous, asymmetrical muzzle bell that dominates the weapon's profile
Four micro-vents along the upper muzzle showing bronze-gold thermal coating
Ferroelectric capacitor housing visible as a subtle ridge along the upper frame with faint LED charge indicator (amber when charged)
Magnetic suspension port on the right side of the frame — a small circular aperture showing precision engineering
Minimal iron sights: notch and post configuration optimized for close-quarters work
Integrated rail on top for optional optics; most field units leave it bare
Magazine well recessed slightly for fumble-free reloading
Distinctive grinding sound grooves etched subtly into the muzzle exterior — deliberate acoustic design
Blackwood Commercial Group stamp on the left frame, small and utilitarian
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Blackwood Commercial Group logo — a stylized geometric mark — stamped in matte silver on the left side of the lower frame; serial plate mounted on the right grip panel, partially obscured by thumb position when held; FESA-2 designation etched in minimal font above the trigger guard
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Scratches and micro-scuffs on the polymer, particularly around the grip and muzzle. The bronze thermal coating shows dueling wear patterns — some areas polished by repeated handling, others darkened by heat cycling. Operators who carry these maintain them religiously; neglect = catastrophic failure. Most examples show signs of regular cleaning and professional care.
